drafted_from: tool:forward-a-fact-to-my-computer's own row (its words, input schema, wakes and invoke), do-work/forward-a-fact.mjs and read-data/forward.json
start_here: Say to your AI: "Forward this Mac's message facts to my always-on computer", with {"to":"my-always-on","door":"https://gateway.example/mcp","forwarded_from":"mac"}. It switches on this tool's wake for that kind with that input, and from then on each fact of that kind this computer hears is told to my-always-on as a sender's fact, once per event id.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: each run tells one fact to one computer and answers what that computer said, and the facts stay in the far computer's own wake book.
instructions: 1. Keep a key made for wake:arrive alone (your sign-in tool's scoped key) in this computer's vault as forward-facts-to-my-computer-key, with your gateway's host as its only host.

2. When the work of one kind moves to the other computer, switch off its wake here and switch on this tool's wake of that kind (wake:switch {tool: "tool:forward-a-fact-to-my-computer", id: "forward-<kind>", on: true, input: {to, door, forwarded_from}}). While a wake of another tool here still hears that kind, the forward refuses each fact, naming it.

3. Read each run's answer in wake:list: kept and heard_by say the far computer took the fact; not_heard says no wake there hears that kind yet; a failed wake names why (a refused key, a computer the gateway does not carry, a gateway that did not answer).
4. On the far computer, the wakes that run from those facts hear them from ["sender"] with match {"forwarded_from": "mac"}, so they hear forwarded facts only.

worked_examples.title: Noticed things heard on a Mac are handled on the always-on computer
worked_examples.ask: Forward this Mac's message facts to my always-on computer.
worked_examples.given: The wake forward-something-showed-up and the input {"to":"my-always-on","door":"https://gateway.example/mcp","forwarded_from":"mac"}, with the noticer's own consumer switched off here; then a something-showed-up fact with event id m-1 is heard on this computer.
worked_examples.hands_back: The switch answers {tool, id: "forward-something-showed-up", on: true}. The run the fact starts answers {"to":"my-always-on","computer":"my-always-on","kind":"something-showed-up","event_id":"m-1","request_key":"fact:m-1","kept":true,"heard_by":1,"starts":"now"}.
